analysis.title: Rates Outlook 2027: Steeper roads ahead
key_insights: ABN AMRO expects a steeper Bund curve in 2027. Front-end yields fall as ECB easing is repriced, while higher supply and term premium keep ultra-long yields elevated.

The 2Y Schatz is forecast to fall about 60bps from current levels to about 2.4% by end-2027. The catalyst is less hawkish ECB communication after the hiking cycle ends at the 18 March meeting, with repricing expected in early Q2 2027.
The 10s30s Bund curve is forecast at about 70bp by end-2027, from about 35bp now. 30Y yields are pushed up by term premium, 10Y yields fall less than 2Y yields.

German net government bond supply is expected to rise about 25% y/y in 2027 versus about 16% in 2026. The fiscal deficit widens from 4.1% of GDP in 2026 to 4.3% in 2027 (consensus 4.2%). About a quarter of the EUR 355bn of 2027 APP and PEPP redemptions are estimated to be German bonds.
German issuance at the 15/20Y and 30Y points has exceeded initial plans by as much as 25% so far in 2026. The 10Y term premium is broadly unchanged since early 2025, the 30Y has edged higher.

The ECB view is two more hikes (December 2026 and March 2027), then a hold, then easing from Q4 2027 to a 2.25% deposit rate by Q2 2028. Markets price two hikes over six months, in line, but do not price the late-2027 and later cuts.

France is the main source of euro-area spread volatility. 10Y OAT-Bund is forecast around 150bp for the first nine months of 2027, tightening toward 125bp by year-end after the presidential and any parliamentary election. Levels above 200bp would need a broader euro-area cohesion challenge.

Italy: BTP-Bund spreads are expected to stay near current wide levels. Italy cannot exit the EU Excessive Deficit Procedure, a EUR 28bn energy and defence package faces uncertain EU approval, NGEU funding ends, and net BTP issuance is expected to rise about 18%. Snap elections as early as April are possible.

Spain: the 29 November snap election is likely to produce a PP-Vox coalition. The deficit fell from 4.6% in 2022 to 2.4% in 2025. Net issuance is expected to rise only about 2% in 2027. 10-15Y SPGBs offer attractive carry and roll.

Belgium: no 2027 budget agreement yet, deficit about 5.2% of GDP in 2025 and projected at about 5.7% by 2028 by the National Bank of Belgium. OLO-Bund spreads are expected to stay around 100bp through at least 1H27, with net issuance up about 30%.

Netherlands: DSL-Bund spreads should stay tight, with 2Y DSLs offering about 15bp of carry and roll. The DSL 2056 has gone from 20.5bp over the reference Bund at issue in September 2025 to almost -2bp. Dutch pension-driven shifts out of cash bonds and flight-to-quality episodes are risks.

US: the markets now price almost three additional Fed hikes over nine months versus one hike in December in ABN AMRO's forecast. Markets price about a 50% chance of a cut by mid-2028, while ABN AMRO expects 75bps of cuts starting in Q4 2027 to a 3.5% upper bound by Q2 2028. 2Y UST repricing is expected from late Q1 or early Q2 2027.

UST curve: lower 2Y yields and steeper 2s10s, with more pronounced steepening in 2s10s than 10s30s. Fiscal concerns, large refinancing needs (debt due within one year is about 30% of GDP) and reduced Fed support keep term premium elevated.

AI-related equity selloffs have pushed UST yields down: AI-capex news moved 2Y and 10Y yields by about 2.5bps and 1.3bps, and a 1% Nasdaq decline is associated with a 2-2.5bp decline in yields. A sustained AI investment bust is not the base case, so such rallies are expected to be temporary.

US midterms: Democrats won both chambers but lack two-thirds majorities, so gridlock is likely. This limits fiscal expansion but does not deliver consolidation. Primary dealers project a deficit of about USD 2.2tn in FY2027 versus USD 2.1tn in FY2026, with privately held net marketable borrowing stable at about USD 2.0-2.1tn.
Debt ceiling: the Bipartisan Policy Center estimates the limit will be reached between late winter and mid-summer 2027. Pressure would fall mainly on bills maturing near the X-date.

The Fed holds about 14% of the UST market, up from a 25-year low of about 13% in December 2025, with balance sheet growth concentrated in bills. A Fed task force on shrinking the balance sheet is due to report to the FOMC in early Q1 2027, per Chair Kevin Warsh. Ending bill purchases would lift short yields, while a 'Reverse Operation Twist' would lift long yields and steepen the curve.

Euro swaps: the 10Y swap spread is forecast at about 10bp in 1H27, narrowing to 5bp from Q3. The 30Y swap spread is expected to widen as the Dutch pension transition removes 30Y hedging demand. Repositioning on 10s30s is estimated at about EUR 110mn DV01, which supports EUR IRS 10s30s steepening.
Across markets: more UST than German 2s10s steepening in 2027, but more German than UST 10s30s steepening on a longer horizon (principally 2028).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Two more hikes (December 2026, March 2027), a hold, then cuts from Q4 2027. Markets price the hikes but not the late-2027 cuts.

macro_indicators.reading: 4.00% now, 4.25% after a December 2026 hike, 3.50% by Q2 2028
macro_indicators.interpretation: One more hike, a hold through the first three quarters of 2027, then 75bps of cuts from Q4 2027. Markets price almost three hikes.
Falls as ECB cuts are priced after a less hawkish shift in communication in early Q2 2027.
Falls as markets price less tightening and more subsequent easing.
Declines less than the 2Y because of elevated term premium.
Ultra-long supply and term premium steepen the curve.
Front-end repricing of Fed easing drives the steepening.

Political and fiscal uncertainty keeps spreads wide until after the elections.

trade_ideas.description: Position for Bund 2s10s and 10s30s steepening in 2027, with lower 2Y Schatz yields
trade_ideas.rationale: ECB cuts get priced from early Q2 2027 while supply and Eurosystem runoff lift term premium at the ultra-long end.
trade_ideas.risk: Markets keep pricing higher for longer through Q1 2027, so 2Y yields may not fall until communication shifts.

trade_ideas.description: Position for UST 2s10s steepening with lower 2Y yields
trade_ideas.rationale: Markets price more Fed hikes and less subsequent easing than ABN AMRO expects, so front-end repricing begins in late Q1 or early Q2 2027.
trade_ideas.risk: Debt-ceiling stress, high refinancing needs or an end to Fed bill purchases could temporarily lift short-end yields.

trade_ideas.description: Position for EUR IRS 10s30s steepening and 30Y swap spread widening
trade_ideas.rationale: Dutch pension hedging shifts from the 30Y point toward the 10Y point with fewer offsetting positions.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher 30Y Bund supply partly restrains the widening in swap spreads.

trade_ideas.description: Own 10-15Y Spanish SPGBs for carry and roll, and 2Y Dutch DSLs for about 15bp of carry and roll
trade_ideas.rationale: Benign Spanish supply (net issuance up about 2%) and low Dutch spread volatility.
trade_ideas.risk: Spanish fiscal slippage under a PP-Vox coalition, Dutch pension-related cash-bond demand and flight-to-quality episodes.

trade_ideas.description: Expect OAT and OLO spreads to stay under pressure, with limited scope for BTP-Bund tightening
trade_ideas.rationale: Political and fiscal uncertainty and higher net issuance (France about 14%, Belgium about 30%, Italy about 18%).
trade_ideas.risk: Greater fiscal or political clarity in France would allow spreads to tighten toward 125bp.

risk_factors: Markets continue to price higher for longer through Q1 2027, delaying the decline in 2Y yields.
French political and fiscal instability, with Belgian spillover. Spreads above 200bp would need a broader euro-area cohesion challenge.
Italian fiscal risk: EDP exit blocked, uncertain EU approval of the EUR 28bn package, possible snap elections and NGEU expiry.
Spanish fiscal slippage if Vox gains substantial influence over a PP-led coalition. Pledges, if fully implemented, could take the deficit toward 5% of GDP by 2030.
US debt ceiling reached between late winter and mid-summer 2027, plus large short-term refinancing needs.
Reduced Fed support if the balance-sheet task force recommends shrinking it, with the outcome depending on whether purchases end or the portfolio's maturity shortens.
Dutch pension-related reduction in cash-bond demand, and severe flight-to-quality episodes affecting Dutch spreads.
An AI investment bust (not the base case) would drive a sustained rally in Treasuries.
Higher German supply and Eurosystem runoff raise term premium at the 30Y point.
vol_and_positioning: Many investors unwound 10s30s euro swap steepener positions after the outbreak of war in Iran in March, and the 10s30s swap curve flattened further in September. With fewer offsetting positions, the next Dutch pension transition wave is expected to have more market impact, mainly at the 30Y point.
Dutch pension transition repositioning on 10s30s is estimated at about EUR 110mn DV01. About a third of the sector by assets has moved to the new framework, and the next wave follows on 1 January.
In late September, French political and fiscal tensions triggered a flight to quality that pushed the 10Y swap spread above 10bp.
geopolitical: France: political and fiscal instability ahead of the presidential election and any subsequent parliamentary election.
Italy: possible snap elections as early as April 2027, with the coalition possibly needing support from Futuro Nazionale.
Spain: 29 November snap election, likely PP-Vox coalition.
Belgium: fragile five-party coalition with no 2027 budget agreement.
US midterms: Democrats won both chambers without a veto-proof majority, implying gridlock.
The outbreak of war in Iran in March led investors to unwind 10s30s euro swap steepeners. The energy shock is cited in the Fed outlook.

tension_points.bull_case: ABN AMRO expects 2Y Schatz and 2Y UST yields to fall as markets move toward its ECB and Fed paths, with repricing triggered by less hawkish central bank communication in early Q2 2027 (late Q1 or early Q2 for the Fed).
tension_points.bear_case: Markets continue to price higher for longer through Q1 2027, so no significant decline in 2Y yields is expected until they converge. Debt-ceiling stress, refinancing needs and an end to Fed bill purchases could lift short-end yields.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No shift to less hawkish ECB communication after the 18 March meeting, or Fed communication staying hawkish into Q2 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher German supply (net issuance up about 25%) and Eurosystem runoff push 30Y term premium up, steepening 10s30s to about 70bp.
tension_points.bear_case: Lower short-rate expectations could outweigh term premium, and Bund safe-haven demand supports Bunds early in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: German ultra-long issuance falling short of expectations, or term premia failing to rise despite higher net supply.

tension_points.bull_case: Greater fiscal clarity after the presidential and any parliamentary election could allow OAT-Bund spreads to tighten toward 125bp by end-2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Political gridlock or looser fiscal policy could push spreads wider, with weak fiscal progress and higher supply keeping them near 150bp in 1H27.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A broader challenge to euro-area cohesion, which would push 10Y OAT-Bund spreads above 200bp.

theme_stances.key_argument: Yield declines concentrate at the front end while term premia keep long-end yields elevated, steepening Bund and UST curves.
theme_stances.evidence: Overall, we expect a steeper Bund curve in 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: Political and fiscal uncertainty means little scope for a meaningful reduction in OAT spreads for the first nine months of 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: we see little scope for a meaningful reduction in uncertainty during at least the first nine months of 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: With fewer offsetting positions, the Dutch pension transition shifts hedging away from 30Y and drives 10s30s steepening in swaps.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect the next wave of the pension transition to have a greater market impact
